findings.title: V2 getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses resource UUID instead of group name
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() (line 122), the lambda iterates over resources of type "Groups" and calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) while also adding groupResource.getId() to the granted set. groupResource.getId() is the resource's internal UUID (a system-generated identifier), but the contract of getGroupIdsWithViewPermission requires group IDs (GroupModel.getId()), which are stored as the resource's name. Two consequences follow: (1) hasPermission does findByName(server, groupId) with the resource UUID, so per-group resources (which are named with the group ID) are never matched and the code always falls through to the all-groups resource check. As a result per-group V2 permissions are effectively ignored when computing the visible-group set. (2) The set returned to callers contains resource UUIDs, not group IDs, so downstream consumers (UsersResource.searchForUser / getUsersCount and BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser) end up storing nonsense values in session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, ...) and passing them to user search/count queries, producing wrong results and silent functional regressions whenever an admin has any level of V2 group VIEW_MEMBERS / MANAGE_MEMBERS permission. The fix should be hasPermission(groupResource.getName(), ...) and granted.add(groupResource.getName()). Existing GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest cases do not exercise the all-groups-level permission path, so they do not detect this regression.

findings.title: Potential NPE when all-groups resource cannot be resolved
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission (lines 144-150), when groupId-specific lookup returns null the code falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...).getResourceTypeResource can return null (e.g. when supportsAuthorizationSchema is false, the resourceType is unknown, or the all-groups resource was never created). That null value is then passed unchecked to policyStore.findByResource(server, resource), which on the common JPA/in-memory store implementations will NPE. A simple null check on the result of getResourceTypeResource, or treating a null return as "no all-groups resource -> no permission", would make the code robust.

findings.title: JavaDoc says getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns a Stream
findings.body: The JavaDoc on GroupPermissionEvaluator.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission (added in this PR, line 144-147) reads "@return Stream of IDs of groups with view permission." but the declared return type (and the implementations in both GroupPermissions and GroupPermissionsV2) is Set<String>. Either the wording "Stream of IDs" is a leftover that should be "Set of IDs", or the return type was meant to be a stream. This is the only contract documentation of a method that several other files depend on, so it should be accurate.
